tours.accountMcp.label: Create and revoke a personal MCP token
tours.accountMcp.summary: Issue a personal MCP access token with a name, permission and project scope, copy it once, then remove it from the token list.
tours.accountMcp.step1.title: Choose API key
tours.accountMcp.step1.description: Personal tokens are issued with the "API key" method. Press "API key".
tours.accountMcp.step2.title: Name the token
tours.accountMcp.step2.description: Enter a name (for example "tutorial-agent"). The permission "Read", the expiry "1 month" and your current project checked under "Selected projects" can stay as they are. Then press "Next".
tours.accountMcp.step3.title: Create the token
tours.accountMcp.step3.description: Press "Create token" to issue the token with this name and the default settings.
tours.accountMcp.step4.title: Copy the token now
tours.accountMcp.step4.description: The token and a ready-to-use mcp.json are shown only this once. Copy them if you need them, then press "Done".
tours.accountMcp.step5.title: Find it in the list and remove it
tours.accountMcp.step5.description: Your new token now appears under "Personal tokens". Press "Remove connection" on that token.
tours.accountMcp.step6.title: Confirm removal
tours.accountMcp.step6.description: Confirm in the dialog. Any client using this token loses access immediately.
tours.accountMcp.step7.title: Check the result
tours.accountMcp.step7.description: Check that the token you created is gone from "Personal tokens". Other tokens, such as the Lumen default, stay as they were.
tours.images.label: Image discovery
tours.images.summary: Explore image search, repositories, tags and verification.
tours.adminImages.label: Image administration
tours.adminImages.summary: Safely inspect images, visibility and verification across projects.
tours.images.step1.title: Image actions
tours.images.step1.description: Use the top upload action to register an image. This guide does not upload or change resources.
tours.images.step2.title: Search and column conditions
tours.images.step2.description: Search always uses regular expressions. Sort with a column heading and select values with its adjacent filter. Refresh preserves these conditions.
tours.images.step3.title: Inspect images and versions
tours.images.step3.description: Inspect repository and tag versions, image identifiers and verification. An empty list can reflect your current search and filters.
tours.vmCreate.label: Create VM
tours.vmCreate.summary: Create an instance with the wizard and watch the deployment process.
tours.volume.label: Create·manage volumes
tours.volume.summary: Create a block volume and explore management actions in the list.
tours.drover.label: Drover clusters
tours.drover.summary: Provision a k3s Kubernetes cluster and get connection details.
tours.waygate.label: Waygate
tours.waygate.summary: Explore servers, clients, and connected networks in the current project.
tours.adminCompute.label: Compute management
tours.adminCompute.summary: Explore instance status·capacity·filters and safe detail views across all projects.
tours.adminStorage.label: Storage management
tours.adminStorage.summary: Explore volume trends·status·filters and entry points to detail views.
tours.adminLibrary.label: Library management
tours.adminLibrary.summary: Explore the reading order from layer builds to profiles·artifacts·consumption status.
tours.adminWaygate.label: Waygate management
tours.adminWaygate.summary: Check Waygate servers and connections for the selected project in the management workspace.
tours.adminNetwork.label: Network management
tours.adminNetwork.summary: Explore project filters and the connection·traffic legends in the global topology.
tours.adminContainers.label: Container management
tours.adminContainers.summary: Safely check all container statuses, resources, and details.
tours.adminKeyManager.label: Key Manager management
tours.adminKeyManager.summary: Explore project-specific Barbican quotas and what management actions do.
tours.adminMonitoring.label: Unified monitoring
tours.adminMonitoring.summary: Explore the cluster summary and how to browse instance metrics.
tours.adminSystem.label: System services
tours.adminSystem.summary: Explore service status by category, API endpoints, and storage pool details.
tours.adminIdentity.label: Identity management
tours.vmCreate.step1.title: Start creating a VM
tours.vmCreate.step1.description: On the instances page, click Create VM to open the instance creation wizard.
tours.vmCreate.step2.title: Select an image
tours.vmCreate.step2.description: Choose an OS image for the selected flavor. GPU flavors recommend verified images with preinstalled drivers; CPU flavors prioritize general images. You can select another image manually. Selecting an image moves to settings.
tours.vmCreate.step3.title: Select a flavor
tours.vmCreate.step3.description: A flavor defines the VM's vCPU · memory · disk specifications. Availability is checked against the project's remaining quota and capacity on a single compute host, including GPUs for GPU flavors. This check does not reserve resources; Nova makes the final placement. Select an available flavor to move automatically to the next step.
tours.vmCreate.step5.title: Check general settings
tours.vmCreate.step5.description: Check the VM name (generated if blank), network, SSH key pair, security groups and root disk size. Beside the capacity, you can enable automatic snapshots and backups. Both are off by default. To enable them, review the schedule, retention and consistency limits for in-use volumes and give consent. Then choose Next.
tours.vmCreate.step6.title: Deploy
tours.vmCreate.step6.description: Review the configuration summary one last time. Clicking "Create VM" starts deployment in this order: create boot volume → create instance.
tours.vmCreate.step7.title: Deployment complete
tours.vmCreate.step7.description: After deployment, find the new VM in the instance list. Click its name to open the details.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.label: Delete a VM from its details
tours.instanceDetailDelete.summary: Create a tut- practice VM with the wizard, then stop and delete it from its detail page.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step1.title: Create a practice VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step1.descrip: This tour first creates a practice VM and then deletes only that VM. Click Create VM to open the wizard.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step2.title: Select a flavor
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step2.descrip: Select an available flavor (vCPU · memory · disk). Selecting one moves to the image step.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step3.title: Select an image
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step3.descrip: Choose an OS image. Selecting an image moves to the settings step.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step4.title: Name the practice VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step4.descrip: Enter a name that starts with tut- (for example tut-vm-delete). The tour deletes only this tut- VM. Keep the other settings and choose Next.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step5.title: Deploy the practice VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step5.descrip: Review the summary, then click Create VM to start the deployment.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step6.title: Find the new VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step6.descrip: When the deployment finishes, the wizard closes and the new tut- VM appears in the instance list. Choose Next to open its detail page.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step7.title: Stop the VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step7.descrip: This is the detail page of the VM you just created. The detail page deletes a VM only after it is stopped. Click Stop.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step8.title: Confirm the stop
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step8.descrip: Read the notice and confirm. Stopping keeps the compute allocation and quota; deleting releases them.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step9.title: Delete the VM
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step9.descrip: Once the VM is stopped, Delete appears. Click Delete. Only the tut- VM created in this tour is deleted.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step10.title: Confirm the deletion
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step10.descri: Check the VM name and any volumes listed as retained, then confirm. Retained volumes are only detached, not deleted.
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step11.title: Deletion complete
tours.instanceDetailDelete.step11.descri: After the deletion you return to the instance list, and the tut- VM is no longer listed.
tours.volume.step1.title: Open volume creation
tours.volume.step1.description: Click + Create volume to open the creation form.
tours.volume.step2.title: Enter volume details
tours.volume.step2.description: Enter the volume name and size (GB), then click "Create". The button is enabled after you enter a name.
tours.volume.step3.title: Manage volumes
tours.volume.step3.description: The new volume has been added to the list. Click its row to open the detail panel, or use the action menu on the right to extend·attach to an instance·delete it.
tours.drover.step1.title: Open cluster creation
tours.drover.step1.description: Click + Create cluster to open the Drover cluster creation form.
tours.drover.step2.title: Cluster name
tours.drover.step2.description: Enter a cluster name. It is generated automatically if left blank.
tours.drover.step3.title: OS type
tours.drover.step3.description: Select the node OS. Click Ubuntu (cloud-init) or CoreOS (Ignition) to continue.
tours.drover.step4.title: Master count
tours.drover.step4.description: Select the control plane configuration. Click 1 (single) or 3 (HA — embedded etcd, API LB created automatically) to continue.
tours.drover.step5.title: Agent count
tours.drover.step5.description: Enter a worker (agent) node count between 0~10.
tours.drover.step6.title: Agent flavor
tours.drover.step6.description: Select the VM specifications for agent nodes. You can leave "Use defaults" selected.
tours.drover.step7.title: Create cluster
tours.drover.step7.description: Clicking "Create" starts VM provisioning and k3s installation.
tours.drover.step8.title: Provisioning progress
tours.drover.step8.description: Progress is shown in real time in this order: create VM → install k3s → complete. When finished, click Close, then download kubeconfig from the list card to connect immediately with kubectl.
tours.adminCompute.step1.title: Compute overview
tours.adminCompute.step1.description: Explore VM status across all projects and administrator query tools. This tour does not create VMs or run bulk actions.
tours.adminCompute.step2.title: Narrow the scope
tours.adminCompute.step2.description: Narrow down instances to investigate with host·project·status·name filters. Changing filters only queries data.
tours.adminCompute.step3.title: Check changes
tours.adminCompute.step3.description: Compare ACTIVE·SHUTOFF·ERROR·SHELVED changes in instance count trends over time.
tours.adminCompute.step4.title: All instances
tours.adminCompute.step4.description: Check project·flavor·host·status. Do not click the bulk start·stop·delete actions below the checkboxes.
tours.adminCompute.step5.title: Open instance details
tours.adminCompute.step5.description: Click the name to open the read-only detail panel.
tours.adminCompute.step6.title: Check details
tours.adminCompute.step6.description: Check general information·network·storage·metrics. Do not click actions such as start·stop·delete; close the panel when finished.
tours.adminStorage.step1.title: Storage overview
tours.adminStorage.step1.description: Safely explore volume trends·status·lists across all projects.
tours.adminStorage.step2.title: Check capacity changes
tours.adminStorage.step2.description: Compare total·in-use·available·error volume counts over time.
tours.adminStorage.step3.title: Status distribution
tours.adminStorage.step3.description: Status cards show counts alongside the current filter.
tours.adminStorage.step4.title: Show available volumes only
tours.adminStorage.step4.description: Click the available card to see the status filter applied to the list. This only runs the query again.
tours.adminStorage.step5.title: Search by project and name
tours.adminStorage.step5.description: Narrow the investigation further by project·status·name.
tours.adminStorage.step6.title: All volumes
tours.adminStorage.step6.description: Read size·project·creation date. Do not click edit·transfer·change status·delete in the action menu on the right.
tours.adminStorage.step7.title: Open volume details
tours.adminStorage.step7.description: Click the name to open the read-only detail panel.
tours.adminStorage.step8.title: Check volume configuration
tours.adminStorage.step8.description: Check type·attachments·metadata. Do not run change·recovery actions; close the panel when finished.
tours.adminLibrary.step1.title: Palimpsest Dockerfile workspace
tours.adminLibrary.step1.description: Explore the flow and existing records for building full roots and changed layers from Dockerfiles and optionally creating SSH VMs.
tours.adminLibrary.step2.title: Dockerfile builds and SSH VMs
tours.adminLibrary.step2.description: Import a Dockerfile from direct input·URL·file·pinned GitHub commit, then check lint·plans·job records·VM execution targets.
tours.adminLibrary.step3.title: Profile records
tours.adminLibrary.step3.description: Check profiles created by Dockerfile builds and the lineage·visibility of existing profiles. Do not save·publish·delete.
tours.adminLibrary.step4.title: Artifact overview
tours.adminLibrary.step4.description: Read sealing·visibility status, inheritance chains, requested packages, and reasons deletion is blocked.
tours.adminLibrary.step5.title: Build overview
tours.adminLibrary.step5.description: Check the build pipeline by type·stage·progress·completion status.
tours.adminLibrary.step6.title: Consumer instances
tours.adminLibrary.step6.description: Check the status and creation time of consumer VMs using a profile. Do not create·delete.
tours.adminNetwork.step1.title: All network connections
tours.adminNetwork.step1.description: Explore connections between networks·routers·VMs·Floating IPs·load balancers across projects.
tours.adminNetwork.step2.title: Narrow the scope by project
tours.adminNetwork.step2.description: Selecting a project only narrows the topology display.
tours.adminNetwork.step3.title: Read the topology
tours.adminNetwork.step3.description: Read search·traffic values·network zones (lanes) together with connection lines.
tours.adminNetwork.step4.title: Open router details
tours.adminNetwork.step4.description: Click a router card to open read-only details.
tours.adminNetwork.step5.title: Gateway and interfaces
tours.adminNetwork.step5.description: Check the external gateway and connected subnets, then click × Close to continue.
tours.adminNetwork.step6.title: Open legend
tours.adminNetwork.step6.description: Open the legend to inspect symbols and connection types. Connection-structure animation is optional and does not represent live packets.
tours.adminContainers.step1.title: All containers
tours.adminContainers.step1.description: Explore container status·image·resources·host across all projects.
tours.adminContainers.step2.title: Read the container list
tours.adminContainers.step3.title: Open container details
tours.adminContainers.step3.description: Click a row to open the read-only detail panel.
tours.adminContainers.step4.title: Configuration and network
tours.adminContainers.step4.description: Check general information and addresses. Do not click start·stop·delete, as these change resources.
tours.adminContainers.step5.title: Check logs
tours.adminContainers.step5.description: Open the logs section to view output only. Close the panel when finished.
tours.adminKeyManager.step1.title: Key Manager quotas
tours.adminKeyManager.step2.title: Read quota values
tours.adminKeyManager.step2.description: Check Secrets·Orders·Containers values and project IDs. -1 means unlimited; 0 means disabled.
tours.adminKeyManager.step3.title: Distinguish change actions
tours.adminKeyManager.step3.description: Set and reset are PUT·DELETE operations that change data, so do not click them in this tutorial.
tours.adminMonitoring.step1.title: Unified monitoring
tours.adminMonitoring.step1.description: Explore the cluster summary and instance metrics in read-only mode.
tours.adminMonitoring.step2.title: Cluster summary
tours.adminMonitoring.step2.description: Check Compute·storage·network·containers·data services·Identity status at a glance.
tours.adminMonitoring.step3.title: Instance metrics tab
tours.adminMonitoring.step3.description: Click the tab to open the list of instances across all projects.
tours.adminMonitoring.step4.title: Search instances
tours.adminMonitoring.step4.description: Narrow the list by name or project ID.
tours.adminMonitoring.step5.title: Open metric details
tours.adminMonitoring.step5.description: Click a row to open the read-only metrics panel.
tours.adminMonitoring.step6.title: Read time series
tours.adminMonitoring.step6.description: Check CPU·memory·network·disk time series, plus GPU time series when a GPU is present. Only change the query interval.
tours.adminSystem.step1.title: Service status
tours.adminSystem.step1.description: Read processes by service category, endpoints, and storage pools.
tours.adminSystem.step2.title: Switch categories
tours.adminSystem.step2.description: Check counts and loading status for services such as Compute·Network·Block Storage.
tours.adminSystem.step3.title: Network agents
tours.adminSystem.step3.description: Click the tab to check Agent Type·Binary·Host·Zone·Alive·Admin State.
tours.adminSystem.step4.title: Read status rows
tours.adminSystem.step4.description: Distinguish up·enabled from down·disabled, and check change times and reasons for disabling.
tours.adminSystem.step5.title: API endpoints
tours.adminSystem.step5.description: Check public·internal·admin URLs by service and region.
tours.adminSystem.step6.title: Endpoint interfaces
tours.adminSystem.step6.description: Check that the interface URLs for the same service point to the correct region.
tours.adminSystem.step7.title: Storage pools
tours.adminSystem.step8.title: Read capacity
tours.adminIdentity.step1.title: Identity user management
tours.adminIdentity.step1.description: Safely explore user summaries·recent changes·search·filters·lists. Do not create or edit.
tours.adminIdentity.step2.title: User overview
tours.adminIdentity.step2.description: Read total·active·inactive counts alongside recent user change logs.
tours.adminIdentity.step3.title: Search and sort
tours.adminIdentity.step3.description: Narrow the list by name·email search, active status, and sorting by name·first activity date.
tours.adminIdentity.step4.title: Show active users only
tours.adminIdentity.step4.description: Selecting active status only changes the client-side list; it does not change user accounts.
tours.adminIdentity.step5.title: User list
tours.adminIdentity.step6.title: Details and session entry points
tours.adminIdentity.step6.description: Clicking a row opens the edit form and session management. In this safe tour, do not click rows·active toggles·save·revoke sessions.
tours.waygate.step1.description: Only Waygate servers in the currently selected project are shown. Switching projects also resets details and selection.
tours.waygate.step2.title: Server list
tours.waygate.step2.description: Check server status and client counts. Click a row to open details.
tours.waygate.step1.title: Network Waygate
tours.adminWaygate.step1.title: Waygate management
start.label: Tutorial
start.inviteDescription: Get step-by-step guidance on how to use this page.
start.hint: You can restart any time with this Tutorial button.
mockup.unsupported: This action is not supported in tutorial mode yet.
tours.buckets.label: Create·delete buckets
tours.buckets.summary: Create an object storage bucket and move it to the trash, step by step.
tours.buckets.step1.title: Open bucket creation
tours.buckets.step1.description: Click + Create bucket to open the creation dialog.
tours.buckets.step2.title: Enter a bucket name
tours.buckets.step2.description: Enter a bucket name, then click Create. The button is enabled once the name is valid.
tours.buckets.step3.title: Check the new bucket
tours.buckets.step3.description: The bucket you just created is now in the list.
tours.buckets.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.buckets.step4.description: Click the Delete button of the bucket you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.buckets.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.buckets.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The bucket moves to the trash.
tours.buckets.step6.title: Moved to trash
tours.buckets.step6.description: A deleted bucket can be restored from the trash or purged permanently.
tours.containers.label: Create·delete containers
tours.containers.summary: Create a Zun container and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.containers.step1.title: Open container creation
tours.containers.step1.description: Click + Create container to open the creation panel.
tours.containers.step2.title: Enter name and image
tours.containers.step2.description: Enter a container name and image, then click Create. The button is enabled once both are filled.
tours.containers.step3.title: Check the new container
tours.containers.step3.description: The container you just created is now in the list.
tours.containers.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.containers.step4.description: Click Delete on the container you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.containers.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.containers.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The container is removed from the list.
tours.containers.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.containers.step6.description: Check that the container is gone from the list.
tours.secrets.label: Create·delete secrets
tours.secrets.summary: Create a Key Manager secret and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.secrets.step1.title: Open secret creation
tours.secrets.step1.description: Click + Create secret to open the creation dialog.
tours.secrets.step2.title: Enter name, type and value
tours.secrets.step2.description: Enter a secret name, choose a type, add a value, then click Create. Tutorial values are never stored or shown.
tours.secrets.step3.title: Check the new secret
tours.secrets.step3.description: The secret you just created is now in the list.
tours.secrets.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.secrets.step4.description: Click Delete on the secret you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.secrets.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.secrets.step5.description: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The secret is removed from the list.
tours.secrets.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.secrets.step6.description: Check that the secret you created is gone from the list. System-managed secrets cannot be deleted.
tours.volumeBackups.label: Create·delete volume backups
tours.volumeBackups.summary: Create a volume backup and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.volumeBackups.step1.title: Open backup creation
tours.volumeBackups.step1.description: Click + Create backup to open the creation dialog.
tours.volumeBackups.step2.title: Choose a volume and name
tours.volumeBackups.step2.description: Choose a volume whose status is available, enter a backup name, then click Create. An in-use volume needs the force option, so the button stays disabled.
tours.volumeBackups.step3.title: Check the new backup
tours.volumeBackups.step3.description: The backup you just created is now in the list.
tours.volumeBackups.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.volumeBackups.step4.description: Click Delete on the backup you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.volumeBackups.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.volumeBackups.step5.description: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The backup is removed from the list.
tours.volumeBackups.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.volumeBackups.step6.description: Check that the backup you created is gone from the list.
tours.iamProjects.label: Create·delete projects
tours.iamProjects.summary: Create a domain project, then delete it after the dependent-resource check, step by step.
tours.iamProjects.step1.title: Open project creation
tours.iamProjects.step1.description: Click Create project to open the creation dialog.
tours.iamProjects.step2.title: Enter a name and create
tours.iamProjects.step2.description: Enter a project name (and a description if you like), then click Create. The button is enabled once a name is entered.
tours.iamProjects.step3.title: Check the new project
tours.iamProjects.step3.description: The project you just created is now in the list.
tours.iamProjects.step4.title: Click Remove
tours.iamProjects.step4.description: Click Remove on the project you just created. The delete dialog opens and first checks for remaining resources.
tours.iamProjects.step5.title: Delete after the check
tours.iamProjects.step5.description: Delete is enabled only after the check shows the project is empty. Click Delete to remove the project.
tours.iamProjects.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.iamProjects.step6.description: Check that the project is gone from the list.
tours.keypairs.label: Create·delete key pairs
tours.keypairs.summary: Create an SSH key pair, check it in the list, and delete it.
tours.keypairs.step1.title: Open key pair creation
tours.keypairs.step1.description: Click + Create key pair to open the creation dialog.
tours.keypairs.step2.title: Enter a name
tours.keypairs.step2.description: Enter a key pair name and click Create. Leave the public key empty to have a new key generated.
tours.keypairs.step3.title: Save the private key
tours.keypairs.step3.description: The generated private key is shown only once. Save it somewhere safe, then click Confirm.
tours.keypairs.step4.title: Delete the new key pair
tours.keypairs.step4.description: The key pair you just created is now in the list. Click its Delete button. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.keypairs.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.keypairs.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The key pair is deleted.
tours.keypairs.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.keypairs.step6.description: Check that the key pair is gone from the list.
tours.floatingIps.label: Allocate·release floating IPs
tours.floatingIps.summary: Allocate a floating IP from an external network, check it in the list, and release it.
tours.floatingIps.step1.title: Open allocation
tours.floatingIps.step1.description: Click Allocate floating IP to open the allocation dialog.
tours.floatingIps.step2.title: Allocate an address
tours.floatingIps.step2.description: Choose an external network if asked, then click Allocate IP. A single external network is selected automatically.
tours.floatingIps.step3.title: Check the new address
tours.floatingIps.step3.description: The new floating IP is now in the list. It is not attached to any instance yet.
tours.floatingIps.step4.title: Click Release
tours.floatingIps.step4.description: Click Release on the address you just allocated. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.floatingIps.step5.title: Confirm release
tours.floatingIps.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The address returns to the external network's pool.
tours.floatingIps.step6.title: Release complete
tours.floatingIps.step6.description: Check that the address is gone from the list.
tours.securityGroups.label: Create·delete security groups
tours.securityGroups.summary: Create a security group, open it from the list, and delete it.
tours.securityGroups.step1.title: Open security group creation
tours.securityGroups.step1.description: Click + Create security group to open the creation dialog.
tours.securityGroups.step2.title: Enter name and description
tours.securityGroups.step2.description: Enter a group name (the description is optional), then click Create. New groups contain only egress rules.
tours.securityGroups.step3.title: Select the new group
tours.securityGroups.step3.description: The group you just created is now in the list. Click it to open its rules panel.
tours.securityGroups.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.securityGroups.step4.description: Click Delete at the top of the rules panel. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.securityGroups.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.securityGroups.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The security group is deleted.
tours.securityGroups.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.securityGroups.step6.description: Check that the group is gone from the list.
tours.networks.label: Create·delete networks
tours.networks.summary: Create a private network and delete it from its actions menu.
tours.networks.step1.title: Open network creation
tours.networks.step1.description: Click + Create network to open the creation dialog.
tours.networks.step2.title: Enter a name and create
tours.networks.step2.description: Enter a network name (for example, tut-network), then click Create. Adding a subnet is optional.
tours.networks.step3.title: Open the actions menu
tours.networks.step3.description: The network you just created is now in the list. Click the actions menu button on its row.
tours.networks.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.networks.step4.description: Click Delete in the menu. A confirmation dialog opens for the network you just created.
tours.networks.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.networks.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The network is deleted.
tours.networks.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.networks.step6.description: Check that the network you just created is gone from the list. Existing networks stay as they are.
tours.volumeSnapshots.label: Create·delete volume snapshots
tours.volumeSnapshots.summary: Create a snapshot of a volume and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step1.title: Open snapshot creation
tours.volumeSnapshots.step1.description: Click + Create snapshot to open the creation dialog.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step2.title: Choose a volume and name
tours.volumeSnapshots.step2.description: Choose an available volume (in the tutorial, scratch), enter a snapshot name, then click Create. An attached volume such as root-disk needs force snapshot turned on.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step3.title: Check the new snapshot
tours.volumeSnapshots.step3.description: The snapshot you just created is now in the list.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.volumeSnapshots.step4.description: Click Delete on the snapshot you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.volumeSnapshots.step5.description: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The snapshot is removed from the list.
tours.volumeSnapshots.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.volumeSnapshots.step6.description: Check that the snapshot you created is gone from the list.
tours.fileStorage.label: Create·delete file storage
tours.fileStorage.summary: Create a Manila file share with the wizard and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.fileStorage.step1.title: Open the creation wizard
tours.fileStorage.step1.description: Click + Create file storage to open the wizard.
tours.fileStorage.step2.title: Enter a name and size
tours.fileStorage.step2.description: Enter a name and choose a size, keep the default share type and protocol, then click Create.
tours.fileStorage.step3.title: File storage created
tours.fileStorage.step3.description: The share is ready. You can add an access rule here, or click Done to close the wizard.
tours.fileStorage.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.fileStorage.step4.description: Click Delete on the file storage you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.fileStorage.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.fileStorage.step5.description: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The file storage is removed from the list.
tours.fileStorage.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.fileStorage.step6.description: Check that the file storage you created is gone from the list.
tours.loadBalancers.label: Create·delete load balancers
tours.loadBalancers.summary: Create a load balancer on a project subnet, check it on its detail page, then delete it.
tours.loadBalancers.step1.title: Open load balancer creation
tours.loadBalancers.step1.description: Click + Create load balancer to open the create page.
tours.loadBalancers.step2.title: Name, network and subnet
tours.loadBalancers.step2.description: Enter a name, pick a project network such as sample-private, then choose its subnet under VIP subnet and click Create. A name and a subnet are both required.
tours.loadBalancers.step3.title: Check the new load balancer
tours.loadBalancers.step3.description: The detail page of the new load balancer is open. Check its status and VIP address. Delete becomes available once provisioning finishes and the status is ACTIVE.
tours.loadBalancers.step4.title: Delete the load balancer
tours.loadBalancers.step4.description: Click Delete on this load balancer. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.loadBalancers.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.loadBalancers.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The load balancer is deleted together with its listeners and pools, and you return to the list.
tours.loadBalancers.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.loadBalancers.step6.description: On the load balancer list, check that the load balancer you created is gone.
tours.routers.label: Create·delete routers
tours.routers.summary: Create a router, open it from the list, then delete it.
tours.routers.step1.title: Open router creation
tours.routers.step1.description: Click + Create router to open the create dialog.
tours.routers.step2.title: Name and gateway
tours.routers.step2.description: Enter a router name. The external network is optional: keep No external gateway, or pick an external network for internet access. Then click Create.
tours.routers.step3.title: Open the new router
tours.routers.step3.description: The new router was added to the list. Click Details on this router to open its panel.
tours.routers.step4.title: Delete the router
tours.routers.step4.description: Click Delete in the router panel. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.routers.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.routers.step5.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The router is deleted and the panel closes.
tours.routers.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.routers.step6.description: Check that the router you created is gone from the list.
tours.containersClusters.label: Create·delete K8s clusters
tours.containersClusters.summary: Create a Magnum K8s cluster and delete it from the list, step by step.
tours.containersClusters.step1.title: Open cluster creation
tours.containersClusters.step1.descripti: Click + Create cluster to open the creation dialog.
tours.containersClusters.step2.title: Enter name, template and node counts
tours.containersClusters.step2.descripti: Enter a cluster name (start with a letter or digit; use only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores). The first cluster template is selected and master and worker counts are 1. Leave the key pair empty and click Create.
tours.containersClusters.step3.title: Check the new cluster
tours.containersClusters.step3.descripti: The cluster you just created was added to the list. It shows CREATE_IN_PROGRESS at first and turns CREATE_COMPLETE after a refresh.
tours.containersClusters.step4.title: Click Delete
tours.containersClusters.step4.descripti: Click Delete on the cluster you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.containersClusters.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.containersClusters.step5.descripti: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The cluster is removed from the list.
tours.containersClusters.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.containersClusters.step6.descripti: Check that the cluster you just created is gone from the list. Existing clusters stay as they are.
tours.databaseInstances.label: Create·delete DB instances
tours.databaseInstances.summary: Create a database instance, check it in the list, and delete it.
tours.databaseInstances.step1.title: Open DB instance creation
tours.databaseInstances.step1.descriptio: Click + Create instance to open the creation dialog.
tours.databaseInstances.step2.title: Enter a name and create
tours.databaseInstances.step2.descriptio: Enter an instance name (for example, tut-db), then click Create. The datastore, version, flavor and volume size are prefilled with defaults.
tours.databaseInstances.step3.title: Check the new instance
tours.databaseInstances.step3.descriptio: The instance you just created is now in the list. Click Next when you have found it.
tours.databaseInstances.step4.title: Delete the instance you created
tours.databaseInstances.step4.descriptio: Click Delete on the row of the instance you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.databaseInstances.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.databaseInstances.step5.descriptio: Click Confirm in the dialog. The instance is deleted.
tours.databaseInstances.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.databaseInstances.step6.descriptio: Check that the instance you just created is gone from the list. Existing instances stay as they are.
tours.databaseBackups.label: Create·delete database backups
tours.databaseBackups.summary: Open a database instance, create a backup from its detail panel, then delete that backup, step by step.
tours.databaseBackups.step1.title: Open a database instance
tours.databaseBackups.step1.description: Click the name of an ACTIVE database instance (in the tutorial, sample-customer-mysql) to open its detail panel. Trove backs up only ACTIVE instances.
tours.databaseBackups.step2.title: Open backup creation
tours.databaseBackups.step2.description: In the Backups section, click + Create backup to open the backup form.
tours.databaseBackups.step3.title: Enter a backup name
tours.databaseBackups.step3.description: In the tutorial, the name field is prefilled with a tut-instance-date-time name. Keep it or enter another name that starts with tut-, optionally add a description, then click Create backup. An empty name also creates a tut- backup.
tours.databaseBackups.step4.title: Check the new backup
tours.databaseBackups.step4.description: The backup you just created is now in the list. It shows NEW at first and can be deleted once it turns COMPLETED after a refresh.
tours.databaseBackups.step5.title: Click Delete
tours.databaseBackups.step5.description: Click Delete on the backup you just created. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.databaseBackups.step6.title: Confirm deletion
tours.databaseBackups.step6.description: Click Confirm in the confirmation dialog. The backup is removed from the list.
tours.databaseBackups.step7.title: Deletion complete
tours.databaseBackups.step7.description: Check that the backup you created is gone from the list. Existing backups stay as they are.
tours.adminProjects.label: Create·delete admin projects
tours.adminProjects.summary: Create a project in the selected domain, then delete it after the dependent-resource check.
tours.adminProjects.step1.title: Open project creation
tours.adminProjects.step1.description: Click + Create to open the project creation dialog. The list shows the projects of the selected domain.
tours.adminProjects.step2.title: Enter a name and create
tours.adminProjects.step2.description: Enter a project name (for example tut-project) and an optional description, then click Create. The button is enabled once a name is entered.
tours.adminProjects.step3.title: Delete the new project
tours.adminProjects.step3.description: The project you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this project. The delete dialog first checks for remaining resources.
tours.adminProjects.step4.title: Delete after the check
tours.adminProjects.step4.description: Delete is enabled only after the check shows the project is empty. Click Delete to remove the project.
tours.adminProjects.step5.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminProjects.step5.description: The result count is updated. Check that the project you created is gone from the list. Existing projects stay as they are.
tours.adminFlavors.label: Create·delete flavors
tours.adminFlavors.summary: Create a flavor with vCPU, RAM and disk sizes, then delete it with confirmation.
tours.adminFlavors.step1.title: Open flavor creation
tours.adminFlavors.step1.description: Click + Create to open the flavor creation dialog.
tours.adminFlavors.step2.title: Enter sizes and create
tours.adminFlavors.step2.description: Enter a flavor name (for example tut-flavor) and the vCPU, RAM (MB) and disk (GB) sizes. Choose Public or Private, then click Create.
tours.adminFlavors.step3.title: Delete the new flavor
tours.adminFlavors.step3.description: The flavor you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this flavor. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminFlavors.step4.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminFlavors.step4.description: Click Confirm in the dialog. The flavor is deleted.
tours.adminFlavors.step5.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminFlavors.step5.description: Check that the flavor you created is gone from the list; you can search by name here. Managed flavors cannot be deleted on this page.
tours.adminRouters.label: Create·delete routers (admin)
tours.adminRouters.summary: Create a router with an optional external gateway, then delete it from the administrator list.
tours.adminRouters.step1.title: Open router creation
tours.adminRouters.step1.description: Click + Create to open the router creation dialog.
tours.adminRouters.step2.title: Name and gateway
tours.adminRouters.step2.description: Enter a router name (for example tut-router). The external network is optional: keep None, or pick an external network. Then click Create.
tours.adminRouters.step3.title: Delete the new router
tours.adminRouters.step3.description: The router you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this router. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminRouters.step4.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminRouters.step4.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The router is deleted.
tours.adminRouters.step5.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminRouters.step5.description: The router count is updated. Check that the router you created is gone from the list. Existing routers stay as they are.
tours.adminFloatingIps.label: Create·delete floating IPs (admin)
tours.adminFloatingIps.summary: Allocate a floating IP from an external network, then delete it from the administrator list.
tours.adminFloatingIps.step1.title: Open floating IP creation
tours.adminFloatingIps.step1.description: Click + Create to open the floating IP creation dialog.
tours.adminFloatingIps.step2.title: Choose the external network
tours.adminFloatingIps.step2.description: Pick the external network to allocate the address from. Then click Create.
tours.adminFloatingIps.step3.title: Delete the new floating IP
tours.adminFloatingIps.step3.description: The floating IP you just allocated is now in the list as Unassigned. Click Delete on this address. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminFloatingIps.step4.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminFloatingIps.step4.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The floating IP is released.
tours.adminFloatingIps.step5.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminFloatingIps.step5.description: The floating IP totals are updated. Check that the address you allocated is gone from the list. Existing floating IPs stay as they are.
tours.adminPorts.label: Create·delete ports (admin)
tours.adminPorts.summary: Create an unbound port on a network, then delete it from the administrator list.
tours.adminPorts.step1.title: Open port creation
tours.adminPorts.step1.description: Click + Create to open the port creation dialog.
tours.adminPorts.step2.title: Network and name
tours.adminPorts.step2.description: Choose the network for the port and enter a name (for example tut-port). The owner project and fixed IP are optional and can stay empty. Then click Next.
tours.adminPorts.step3.title: Create the port
tours.adminPorts.step3.description: Click Create. The port is created with an automatically assigned address.
tours.adminPorts.step4.title: Delete the new port
tours.adminPorts.step4.description: The port you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this port. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminPorts.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminPorts.step5.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The port is deleted.
tours.adminPorts.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminPorts.step6.description: The port count is updated. Check that the port you created is gone from the list. Existing ports stay as they are.
tours.adminRoles.label: Create·delete roles (admin)
tours.adminRoles.summary: Create a custom role from an area and a grade, then delete it from its detail panel.
tours.adminRoles.step1.title: Open role creation
tours.adminRoles.step1.description: Click Create role to open the role creation dialog. The button becomes available once the role list has loaded.
tours.adminRoles.step2.title: Area and grade
tours.adminRoles.step2.description: Enter an area (for example tut-role) and a grade (for example viewer). The role name is composed as area_grade, here tut-role_viewer, and is shown below the fields. Description and domain ID are optional and can stay empty. Then click Next.
tours.adminRoles.step3.title: Create the role
tours.adminRoles.step3.description: Click Create. The new role starts without parent or child roles.
tours.adminRoles.step4.title: Open the new role
tours.adminRoles.step4.description: The role you just created is now in the list. Click its name to open the role details.
tours.adminRoles.step5.title: Delete the new role
tours.adminRoles.step5.description: Click Delete role in the detail panel. A confirmation dialog opens. Core roles, retired roles and linked roles cannot be deleted.
tours.adminRoles.step6.title: Enter the role name
tours.adminRoles.step6.description: Type the exact role name (for example tut-role_viewer) to confirm. Delete permanently becomes available when the name matches. Then click Next.
tours.adminRoles.step7.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminRoles.step7.description: Click Delete permanently. The role is deleted.
tours.adminRoles.step8.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminRoles.step8.description: The role count is updated. Check that the role you created is gone from the list. Existing roles stay as they are.
tours.adminDomains.label: Create·disable domains (admin)
tours.adminDomains.summary: Create a domain, then disable it from the domain list. Afterglow does not delete domains.
tours.adminDomains.step1.title: Open domain creation
tours.adminDomains.step1.description: Click Create domain to open the domain dialog.
tours.adminDomains.step2.title: Domain name
tours.adminDomains.step2.description: Enter a name (for example tut-domain). The description is optional. Keep Enable domain checked. Then click Next.
tours.adminDomains.step3.title: Create the domain
tours.adminDomains.step3.description: Click Save. The domain is created and appears in the list as Enabled.
tours.adminDomains.step4.title: Edit the new domain
tours.adminDomains.step4.description: The domain you just created is now in the list. Click Edit on this domain.
tours.adminDomains.step5.title: Disable the domain
tours.adminDomains.step5.description: Clear Enable domain. Users of a disabled domain can no longer sign in. Then click Next.
tours.adminDomains.step6.title: Save the change
tours.adminDomains.step6.description: Click Save. The domain is disabled.
tours.adminDomains.step7.title: Domain disabled
tours.adminDomains.step7.description: The domain you created now shows Disabled. Afterglow does not delete domains; you can enable it again with Edit. Existing domains stay as they are.
tours.adminUsers.label: Create·delete users (admin)
tours.adminUsers.summary: Create a user account, then delete it from the user list after confirming its full ID.
tours.adminUsers.step1.title: Open user creation
tours.adminUsers.step1.description: Click + Create to open the user creation dialog.
tours.adminUsers.step2.title: Name, email and password
tours.adminUsers.step2.description: Enter a name (for example tut-user), an email (for example tut-user@example.test) and a practice password of at least 12 characters. This is a tutorial: the password is not stored and no real account is created. Then click Next.
tours.adminUsers.step3.title: Create the user
tours.adminUsers.step3.description: Click Create. Only the sign-in identity is created; the personal project is prepared at the first sign-in.
tours.adminUsers.step4.title: Check the result
tours.adminUsers.step4.description: The dialog shows the new user ID and its sign-in domain. Click Close.
tours.adminUsers.step5.title: Delete the new user
tours.adminUsers.step5.description: The user you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this user. The directory is reread and a confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminUsers.step6.title: Type the full user ID
tours.adminUsers.step6.description: Deleting an account cannot be undone, so the dialog asks for the full user ID. Type the ID shown above into Full user ID. Delete becomes available when it matches exactly. Then click Next.
tours.adminUsers.step7.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminUsers.step7.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The account is deleted; projects and resources are not.
tours.adminUsers.step8.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminUsers.step8.description: The user overview is updated. Check that the user you created is gone from the list. Existing users stay as they are.
tours.adminGroups.label: Create·delete groups (admin)
tours.adminGroups.summary: Create a user group in the selected domain, then delete it from the group list.
tours.adminGroups.step1.title: Open group creation
tours.adminGroups.step1.description: Click + Create to open the group creation dialog. The list shows the groups of the selected domain.
tours.adminGroups.step2.title: Group name
tours.adminGroups.step2.description: Enter a group name (for example tut-group). The description is optional and can stay empty. Then click Next.
tours.adminGroups.step3.title: Create the group
tours.adminGroups.step3.description: Click Create. The group is created in the selected domain without members.
tours.adminGroups.step4.title: Delete the new group
tours.adminGroups.step4.description: The group you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this group. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminGroups.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminGroups.step5.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The group is deleted.
tours.adminGroups.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminGroups.step6.description: The group count is updated. Check that the group you created is gone from the list. Existing groups stay as they are.
tours.adminAnnouncements.label: Send·delete announcements (admin)
tours.adminAnnouncements.summary: Write and send an announcement, then delete it from the send history.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step1.title: Enter title and body
tours.adminAnnouncements.step1.descripti: Enter a title (for example, tut-notice) and a body. Both are required. Click Next when you are done.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step2.title: Severity and target
tours.adminAnnouncements.step2.descripti: Choose the severity and target. With the defaults (Information · All), every user sees it. Click Next.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step3.title: Send the announcement
tours.adminAnnouncements.step3.descripti: Click Send announcement. It is not sent if the title or body is empty.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step4.title: Delete the announcement you sent
tours.adminAnnouncements.step4.descripti: The announcement you just sent is now in the send history. Click its delete button. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminAnnouncements.step5.descripti: Click Confirm in the dialog. The announcement is deleted.
tours.adminAnnouncements.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminAnnouncements.step6.descripti: Check that the announcement you just sent is gone from the send history. Existing announcements stay as they are.
tours.adminApplicationCredentials.label: Issue·delete application credentials (admin)
tours.adminApplicationCredentials.summar: Issue an application credential that delegates roles from your current admin token, then delete it from the list.
The domain and user (you, the current administrator) are selected. Click Create to open the issue dialog.
Enter name and roles, then save
Enter a name (for example, tut-credential), check at least one role to delegate, then click Save. The description and expiry are optional.
The issued secret is shown only this once. In real use, store it somewhere safe. Click Close.
The credential you just issued is now in the list. Click Delete on its row.
Click Delete in the dialog. The credential is deleted.
Check that the credential you just issued is gone from the list. Existing credentials stay as they are.
tours.adminObjectStorage.label: Create·delete buckets (admin)
tours.adminObjectStorage.summary: Create an object storage bucket in your current project, then move it to trash from the administrator inventory.
tours.adminObjectStorage.step1.title: Open bucket creation
tours.adminObjectStorage.step1.descripti: Click + Create bucket to open the bucket creation dialog. The bucket is created in the project you are signed in to.
tours.adminObjectStorage.step2.title: Name the bucket
tours.adminObjectStorage.step2.descripti: Enter a name (for example tut-bucket): 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Then click Create.
tours.adminObjectStorage.step3.title: Delete the new bucket
tours.adminObjectStorage.step3.descripti: The bucket you just created is now in the list. Click Delete on this bucket. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminObjectStorage.step4.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminObjectStorage.step4.descripti: Click Confirm in the dialog. The bucket moves to trash.
tours.adminObjectStorage.step5.title: Moved to trash
tours.adminObjectStorage.step5.descripti: The bucket now shows Awaiting restoration. It can be restored during the retention period and is deleted permanently when it expires. Existing buckets stay as they are.
tours.adminNetworks.label: Create·delete networks (admin)
tours.adminNetworks.summary: Create a network with an optional subnet, then delete it from the row menu.
tours.adminNetworks.step1.title: Open network creation
tours.adminNetworks.step1.description: Click + Create to open the network creation dialog.
tours.adminNetworks.step2.title: Name and options
tours.adminNetworks.step2.description: Enter a network name (for example tut-network). CIDR is optional and creates a subnet automatically. Leave External network and Shared unchecked, then click Create.
tours.adminNetworks.step3.title: Open the row menu
tours.adminNetworks.step3.description: The network you just created is now in the list. Click the ⋯ menu on this network.
tours.adminNetworks.step4.title: Choose Delete
tours.adminNetworks.step4.description: Click Delete in the menu. A confirmation dialog opens.
tours.adminNetworks.step5.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminNetworks.step5.description: Click Delete in the dialog. The network is deleted.
tours.adminNetworks.step6.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminNetworks.step6.description: The result count is updated. Check that the network you created is gone from the list. Existing networks stay as they are.
tours.adminUserCredentials.label: Register·delete user credentials (admin)
tours.adminUserCredentials.summary: Register an EC2 or certificate credential for a user in the selected domain, then safely delete it from the list.
tours.adminUserCredentials.step1.title: Open credential registration
tours.adminUserCredentials.step1.descrip: The domain scope is verified. Click Create to open the user credential registration dialog.
tours.adminUserCredentials.step2.title: Enter user, type, and data, then save
tours.adminUserCredentials.step2.descrip: Select the target user, enter the credential type (such as ec2) and data (JSON blob), then click Save. The project ID is optional.
tours.adminUserCredentials.step3.title: Delete the credential you created
tours.adminUserCredentials.step3.descrip: The credential you just registered is now in the list. Click Delete on its row for safe cleanup.
tours.adminUserCredentials.step4.title: Confirm deletion
tours.adminUserCredentials.step4.descrip: Click Delete in the warning dialog. The credential is permanently removed.
tours.adminUserCredentials.step5.title: Deletion complete
tours.adminUserCredentials.step5.descrip: Check that the credential you registered is gone from the list. Existing user credentials stay as they are.
tours.adminSettings.label: Tour general settings (admin)
tours.adminSettings.summary: Walk through the six General settings tabs and what each controls. Read-only: nothing is changed or saved.
tours.adminSettings.step1.title: General settings tabs
tours.adminSettings.step1.description: This page has six tabs: Branding, Infrastructure defaults, Enrollment policy, Default quotas, Signup requests and Email. This tour only explains them; it never saves, uploads, approves or sends anything. Click Next.
tours.adminSettings.step2.title: Branding
tours.adminSettings.step2.description: Branding sets the light and dark sign-in logos everyone sees. You upload or reset a logo only from this panel. Click the Infrastructure defaults tab.
tours.adminSettings.step3.title: Infrastructure defaults
tours.adminSettings.step3.description: Choose the default external network, router, storage and other resources Afterglow uses, plus a few runtime settings. A change applies only when you save it in this panel. Click the Enrollment policy tab.
tours.adminSettings.step4.title: Enrollment policy
tours.adminSettings.step4.description: Controls public email signup, whether the signup link shows on the login page, and whether new accounts are approved automatically or by an administrator. This tab shares one save with Default quotas. Click the Default quotas tab.
tours.adminSettings.step5.title: Default quotas
tours.adminSettings.step5.description: Sets the quotas given to future personal projects (-1 unlimited, 0 none, blank native default). It is saved together with Enrollment policy, so review both tabs first. Click the Signup requests tab.
tours.adminSettings.step6.title: Signup requests
tours.adminSettings.step6.description: Lists signup requests waiting for review, where you approve or reject each one. A decision is recorded for that single request and is not replayed. This tour does not touch it. Click the Email tab.
tours.adminSettings.step7.title: Email
tours.adminSettings.step7.description: Configures SMTP and IMAP mail settings, connection checks, a test message and notifications. It has its own save, separate from the other tabs. Click Next.
tours.adminSettings.step8.title: There is no global save
tours.adminSettings.step8.description: Switching tabs keeps your edits and never saves automatically. Branding, Infrastructure defaults and Email apply from their own panels; Enrollment policy and Default quotas share one save. The tour is finished.
tours.adminSystemAdmins.label: Tour system administrators (admin)
tours.adminSystemAdmins.summary: Review the system administrator list and the authority policy. Read-only: nothing is granted or revoked.
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step1.title: Add button
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step1.descriptio: Add opens a dialog that grants platform-wide (system:all) administrator authority to a user in the selected domain. The tour never clicks it; review and make any authority change yourself.
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step2.title: Authority policy
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step2.descriptio: Shows the current number of system administrators and the authority scope. Revoking is blocked when only one administrator remains.
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step3.title: System administrator list
tours.adminSystemAdmins.step3.descriptio: These are the current system administrators. Revoke on a row removes authority immediately, with a confirmation when you revoke yourself. The tour clicked nothing and changed nothing.
